question: Can LLM function calling be made asynchronous so the LLM keeps generating while calls execute, cutting end-to-end task completion latency without hurting call accuracy?
hypothesis: Overlapping function-call generation and execution via in-flight interrupts lowers latency versus synchronous (and synchronous-parallel) calling while keeping accuracy.
contributions: CML, a token-efficient in-context protocol ([CALL], [INTR], [TRAP], [END], [HEAD]) for asynchronous function calls and interrupts
A fine-tuning strategy that teaches LLMs to emit async calls, handle interrupts and emit traps
An inference-side implementation (token monitor, executor, interrupt manager, trap handler) plus a Chat-Completion-API emulation
Latency analysis with theorems for Async vs Sync and the LPT heuristic, and evaluation on BFCL tasks

method.summary: AsyncLM intercepts autoregressive decoding: a CML parser spots function calls, runs them in background workers, and the interrupt manager injects [INTR] result blocks into the token stream when not inside a call block (critical section). Llama-3.2 1B/3B are fine-tuned on simulated DAG traces scheduled with longest-processing-time-first; GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini are adapted by one-shot prompting.
method.task: function calling (latency and AST-match accuracy) on BFCL

datasets.name: BFCL v1-parallel + v2-parallel-live
datasets.split: part of 800 total; 200 for fine-tuning, 600 for evaluation
datasets.source: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (Yan et al., 2024)
datasets.preprocessing: DAGs of function calls extracted by a Python program; estimated execution times 1 ms to 1 s assigned randomly per simulation run

datasets.name: v3-multi-step-parallel (new)
datasets.source: built by randomly combining three multi-step samples from the first round of v3-base-multi-turn

datasets.name: Training traces (task descriptions and function definitions from public function-calling datasets)
datasets.split: inferred: the 200 fine-tuning samples of the 800
datasets.source: BFCL, ToolSandbox (Lu et al. 2024), tau-bench (Yao et al. 2024) cited as trace sources
datasets.preprocessing: user-triggered interrupts also injected from multi-turn conversation datasets (not detailed)

training.objective: inferred: supervised fine-tuning on simulated ideal LLM-executor traces (CML calls, interrupts, traps) so as to minimise makespan; paper states the objective as minimising total task completion time with LPT call ordering
training.hardware: NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU (local deployment, inference and function execution on same machine; fine-tuning hardware not stated)

other.fine_tune_config: default configurations in LlamaFactory (Zheng et al., 2024)
other.simulated_exec_time: 1 ms to 1 s random per call per run
other.simulated_TPOT: random 5 ms to 30 ms per simulation

inference.decoding: next-token distribution constrained by a finite-state machine to valid CML syntax; [INTR] token blocked so the model cannot hallucinate interrupts (Geng et al., 2023 grammar-constrained decoding)
inference.prompting: function definitions as JSON in prompt with estimated completion times; GPT-4o models: one example per dataset plus detailed instructions on interpreting CML; latency runs include a 'cheat sheet' with ground-truth answers in the prompt

parameters.trap_handler_rule: keep KV cache in GPU if both recompute and swap time exceed estimated wait; else recompute if recompute latency lower, else swap
parameters.cloud_Async_emulation: 5 ms per output token from OpenAI API statistics (emulated, not measured)
parameters.function_exec_time: measured 30 ms to 500 ms, average 110 ms

other.serving: Text-Generation-Interface (Hugging-Face, 2023) for local models; implementation on Python transformers library
other.Async-Naive: chat completion API, new request per interrupt, previous session discarded

metrics.name: Task completion latency
metrics.definition: time between the first and last token generation, end to end
metrics.unit: ms (speedups as x relative to Sync)

metrics.name: Function composition accuracy (AST matching)
metrics.definition: exact AST match of each function call to ground truth, plus execution order

baselines: Sync-Parallel (parallel function calling, OpenAI 2023; Kim et al. 2023)
Async-Naive (chat completion API without serving changes)
eval.protocol: Latency figures have error bars of 10th to 90th percentile; number of runs and seeds not stated; no significance tests; Async cloud latency is emulated

availability.data: BFCL is public; the new v3-multi-step-parallel dataset is not stated as released

evidence.quote: From the total of 800 samples, we use 200 for fine-tuning and the remaining 600 for evaluation.

results.claim: AsyncLM cuts end-to-end task completion latency by up to 5.4x versus synchronous function calling across BFCL tasks.
results.setup: v3-multi-step-parallel, local Llama-3B, Async vs Sync
results.quote: AsyncLM can reduce end-to-end task completion latency from 1.6×-5.4× compared to synchronous
results.note: Per Fig 6 text the 5.4x is the local setting; Fig 6 shows 3.2x, 1.6x, 1.7x, 1.8x, 5.4x, 2.4x annotations

results.claim: On simple parallel calls, Async is 1.6x faster than Sync locally and 2.1x on cloud.
results.setup: v1-parallel and v2-parallel-live, local Llama-3B; cloud GPT-4o 2.1x is emulated at 5 ms/token
results.quote: Async completes tasks faster than Sync by 1.6×
results.note: cloud 2.1x: 'for the local deployment and 2.1× for cloud'

results.claim: On the same parallel tasks, Sync-Parallel is 1.3x faster than Sync locally and 1.7x on cloud.
results.quote: Sync-Parallel is 1.3× faster than Sync for local and 1.7×

results.claim: In multi-step parallel tasks Sync-Parallel reduces latency by 3.2x over Sync; Async goes further.
results.setup: v3-multi-step-parallel, three independent tasks of 1-5 sequential calls each
results.quote: while Sync-Parallel reduces latency by 3.2× compared to Sync.

results.claim: Fine-tuned Llama-3B reaches 65.97% AST accuracy under Async versus 57.33% under Sync.
results.setup: multi-step parallel dataset, Llama-3B fine-tuned (FT); Sync in CML is 66.07%
results.table: Table 1, row LLAMA-3B (FT), columns SYNC / ASYNC: 57.33% / 65.97%
results.note: Sync-in-CML 66.07% suggests the gain comes from CML fine-tuning format, not asynchrony

results.claim: GPT-4o with few-shot prompting keeps accuracy under Async (59.61%) versus Sync (57.84%).
results.table: Table 1, row GPT-4O (ICL), columns SYNC / ASYNC: 57.84% / 59.61%

results.claim: Few-shot prompted small models degrade under Async: GPT-4o-mini 55.08% to 41.44%, Llama-3B 16.98% to 5.46%.
results.setup: GPT-4o-mini (ICL), multi-step parallel; Llama-3B ICL 16.98 to 5.46

results.claim: Async adds about 20 tokens on average versus Sync, costing about 90 ms and 27.5 MB extra KV cache on the 3B model (under 5% of memory).
results.quote: Async incurs an average of 20 additional tokens compared to Sync

results.claim: Async-Naive on the OpenAI API is impractical: 1.5x higher latency than Sync-Parallel due to 310 ms average TTFT per interrupt.
results.setup: GPT-4o Async-Naive, new API request per interrupt

results.claim: LPT scheduling is 8% faster on average than choosing the next function at random.
results.note: LPT not optimal with dependencies (NP-hard scheduling); counterexample a,b,c given

results.claim: With tasks arriving as user-triggered interrupts, Async reduces latency 2.4x versus Sync while Sync-Parallel gets only 1.1x.
results.setup: multi-step parallel tasks injected as interrupts at 0, 200, 400 ms
results.quote: latency by 2.4× compared to Sync, whereas Sync-Parallel
results.note: Fig 8 annotations include 5.3x for the other (cloud) bar

results.claim: Theory: Async latency is at most Sync-Parallel latency, which is below Sync latency, for independent functions.
results.setup: assumes same generated token count and no overhead beyond G and E; proof sketches in Appendix A
results.note: Theorem 6.2 estimates speedup about 1 + E/G (avg exec time over avg generation time) for large |F| assuming normal E

limits: Latency evaluation puts ground-truth answers in the prompt (cheat sheet) to avoid biases from wrong calls; the official BFCL accuracy is 62% for GPT-4o and 43% for Llama-3.2-3B
Cloud (GPT-4o) Async latency is emulated from 5 ms/token, not measured; Async-Naive on real API is slower than Sync-Parallel
Few-shot Llama and GPT-4o-mini lose accuracy under Async; fine-tuned Llama gain is matched by Sync-in-CML so asynchrony itself is accuracy-neutral at best
LPT is not guaranteed optimal with dependencies (NP-hard); theory covers independent functions only
Fine-tuning hyperparameters, seeds, run counts and code release are not stated; training set is 200 simulated samples; assumes finite calls per task
Workload is BFCL with function times 30-500 ms; short-execution tasks benefit little (speedup about 1 + E/G)
Human-LLM and LLM-LLM interrupt applications are discussed only briefly; user-triggered dataset details not given

terms.definition: a simple domain-specific language to represent asynchronous function calls and interrupts
[INTR] id [HEAD] value [END] block the executor inserts at the end of the token stream when a call with a registered identifier completes
self-initiated interrupt [TRAP][END] that notifies the serving system the LLM is pausing until a function result arrives
flag, false while a function call block is being generated, that defers interrupts until the LLM exits the block
Longest-Processing-Time-first: call the ready function with the longest estimated execution time
